description:
FILED s451w, from the #694 probes.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on 718db6b and on
the f937afd pre-round-9 base).

    my $w = "world";
    print "Q2=[", <<`H`, "]";
    echo hi $w
    H
        perl: Q2=[hi world\n]        PCL: Q2=[echo hi world\n]

The heredoc INTERPOLATES correctly; it is the EXECUTION that is missing.  A
`<<`TAG`` heredoc is `qx` with a heredoc body -- perl runs the interpolated
text through the shell and the value is the child's stdout.  PCL's heredoc arm
(`Pl::PExpr`, the `heredoc_is_raw` branch around PExpr.pm:950) routes an
interpolating heredoc to `parse_interpolated_string` and returns the resulting
string node; nothing looks at whether the heredoc's TERMINATOR was
backtick-quoted, so `<<`H`` is lowered exactly like `<<"H"`.  The sibling
`` `â¦` `` / `qx{â¦}` arm a few lines above DOES build a `backtick` node.

SEVERITY: silent wrong, and the value flows onward (rule 12) -- a program that
captures a command's output gets the command LINE instead.

WHERE PPI PUTS IT: `PPI::Token::HereDoc` carries the terminator with its
quotes; `Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::heredoc_is_raw` is the existing shared
predicate for the `<<'â¦'` form and is the natural place for a
`heredoc_is_command` sibling (rule 11) -- note `heredoc_is_raw` was itself
written because a hand-rolled `/^<<'/` read `<< 'E'` and `<<~'E'` wrongly
(#301), so the new predicate must handle `<< `E` `, `<<~`E`` and `<<`E`` alike.
The lowering is then the SAME `backtick` node the `` `â¦` `` arm builds, with
the interpolated string as its child.

MEASURED SIDE EFFECT ON A COMPANION ROW: t/op/exec.t row 32
(`<<`119827`` with `sub readpipe { pop }` in scope) PASSES today BY ACCIDENT --
PCL returns the interpolated text and the file's override happens to be the
identity, so "ls\n" comes out either way.  Fixing this task will make that row
depend on #703 (the readpipe override) instead.

BAR: the three-line probe above vs perl; `<<~`H`` and `<< `H` ` spellings; the
`<<'H'` and `<<"H"` inverses unchanged; a guard row; op/exec.t's snapshot row
re-read together with #703.
CLOSED s451z.  `Pl::PExpr::TokenUtils::heredoc_is_command` is the sibling of
heredoc_is_raw (same `/^<<~?\s*/` latitude), and ONE builder,
`Pl::PExpr::_make_command_node`, now serves the `` `â¦` ``/qx arm AND the
heredoc arm.  Probed vs 5.40.3: `` <<`H` ``, `` <<~`H` ``, `` << `H` `` all
execute; `<<"H"` and `<<'H'` unchanged; bodies with quotes, tabs, `;`, and a
trailing `. "tail"` identical.  Guard `Pl/t/system-block-01.t` 11 -> 24 rows.
Emission A/B over 1036 files: op/exec.t the only mover (with #703).

RESIDUE, filed: the LIST-context answer is still one string (#731) -- probe
row E/F of p702c, `my @out = <<`H`` gives 1 element where perl gives 2.
subject: A BACKTICK HEREDOC (`<<`END`) is never executed -- PCL returns its interpolated TEXT as the value where perl runs it and returns the output (silent wrong)
